quarterly_data.quarter: GE Vernova Morgan Stanley laguna conference 2026 (09-16-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CEO Scott Strazik: backlog was $176 billion at the end of the second quarter and, 'on the strength of the orders we expect to see in the third quarter, that $200 billion milestone we should hit very early in 2027' (earlier framed as reaching $200 billion in 2027); he called $200 billion 'a very humble milestone'. He expects a 'very strong third-quarter orders performance' as customers keep converting slot reservation agreements into orders. A 2027 financial outlook will be given on the January earnings call, and a 2030 financial outlook at the next Capital Markets Day, expected in the spring, 'certainly before the summer'.
quarterly_data.figure: $200 billion backlog milestone very early in 2027 (from $176 billion at end of second quarter)

quarterly_data.quarter: GE Vernova Morgan Stanley laguna conference 2026 (09-16-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Gas turbine output ladder (CEO Scott Strazik): GE Vernova has installed over 350 new machines into its gas factories over generally the last 18 months and will 'grow our gas capacity additions by 50% over the course of this year'. It will hit the five-gigawatt run rate for the third and fourth quarter of this year, the beginning of next year will be similar, then step to six gigawatts a quarter sometime in the second half of next year; in 2028 it may stay at six gigawatts for a period before the next step to seven gigawatts a quarter - all within the same factory footprint (automation and robotics, no greenfield). CEO: 'if we perform at our best, we can pull those numbers left.'
quarterly_data.figure: over 350 new machines in 18 months; five gigawatts a quarter in third and fourth quarter; six gigawatts a quarter in second half of next year; seven gigawatts a quarter after 2028 step

quarterly_data.quarter: GE Vernova Morgan Stanley laguna conference 2026 (09-16-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Gas slots since the late-July Q2 call (CEO Scott Strazik): GE Vernova has sold multiple slots for 2032 deliveries 'with cash committed', though 2032 is still single-digit gigawatts of commitments. Over the summer it added 12 incremental gigawatts of supply in 2030 and 2031, sold at premium pricing, and all 12 gigawatts is 'in some form of contracting', most of it likely contracted in the fourth quarter rather than the third. After 40 gigawatts of new contract commitments in the first half, the ~20 gigawatts guided for the second half 'is likely to prove to be conservative', but the company will not run at a 40-gigawatt pace every six months; the fourth quarter should add more than the third. Also seeing 'a lot of traction' with the 7E heavy-duty gas turbine (a 90-megawatt unit); aeroderivatives (30-35-megawatt) suit behind-the-meter data-center applications, while he believes 'over time ... a large majority of these data centers will be grid connected', with customers hoping for interconnects 5-7 years out.
quarterly_data.figure: 12 incremental gigawatts added for 2030 and 2031, all in contracting; 40 gigawatts contracted in first half; 20 gigawatts second-half guide likely conservative; 2032 slots sold (single-digit gigawatts)

quarterly_data.quarter: GE Vernova Morgan Stanley laguna conference 2026 (09-16-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Pricing / margin in backlog (CEO Scott Strazik): the change in margin in backlog in Power for 2026 is expected to be larger than in 2025, when it was 'low double digits'; Electrification's change will be 'more humble' - it was 4 points last year and 'probably something similar to that, maybe a little bit larger' - with pricing power most pronounced in integrated power-gen plus electrification solutions; a healthy positive change is expected in Wind. Most of that equipment delivers in 2029 and 2030, so 'the margin expansion in our business is simply going to continue in the out years'. The 2026 change in equipment margin in backlog will be shown on the January earnings call.
quarterly_data.figure: Power 2026 change in margin in backlog above 2025's low double digits; Electrification about 4 points or a little larger

quarterly_data.quarter: GE Vernova Morgan Stanley laguna conference 2026 (09-16-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Services annuity (CEO Scott Strazik): HA services revenue is about $1 billion of the Power business's $24 billion of revenue, from only 130 machines running today; 195 more machines are on contract and by the end of next year there will cumulatively be at least 400 machines running or on contract - about 200 gigawatts of incremental power. Every gigawatt of HAs generates half a billion dollars of high-margin services revenue over its first 20 years, so by the end of next year GE Vernova will have contracted $100 billion of future services revenue. He called the December 2025 target of Power Services revenue growing from $12 billion in 2025 to $22 billion in 2035 'a conservative marker'.
quarterly_data.figure: HA services about $1 billion of $24 billion Power revenue; 130 HA running, 195 on contract, at least 400 by end of next year; $100 billion of future services revenue contracted; Power Services $12 billion (2025) to $22 billion (2035) called conservative

quarterly_data.quarter: GE Vernova Morgan Stanley laguna conference 2026 (09-16-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Electrification and data centers (CEO Scott Strazik): Electrification backlog has grown from $6 billion at GE Vernova's launch (end of 2021) to $45 billion today. Data-center orders were about $2 billion in 2025 and north of $5 billion in the first half of 2026 - almost 40% of Electrification's orders - but will likely be 'more like 20%' of Electrification orders in 3Q and 4Q because they are lumpy, while backlog keeps growing. New products not in that backlog: multiple Energy Management System (EMS) orders in the first half with more expected; the launch order for the MV-UPS is expected in the second half of the year; the 5-megawatt indoor solid-state transformer is built and the 6-megawatt outdoor unit is in engineering, with SST orders 'more of a 2027 opportunity'. Hyperscalers have racks at GE Vernova's Niskayuna, New York research center connected to its equipment to co-create future products, and Electrification R&D is growing faster than the other two segments.
quarterly_data.figure: Electrification backlog $45 billion (from $6 billion at launch); data-center orders north of $5 billion in first half, about 20% of Electrification orders expected in 3Q and 4Q; MV-UPS launch order expected in second half

quarterly_data.quarter: GE Vernova Morgan Stanley laguna conference 2026 (09-16-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: HVDC and Prolec GE (CEO Scott Strazik): strong HVDC order growth outside the U.S.; GE Vernova was publicly named winner of a large HVDC project in India, 'almost a $1.5 billion transaction in isolation', which will be booked as an order in the fourth quarter. Prolec GE integration: 'even more opportunity to fulfill within the existing footprint than I anticipated' at the Shreveport, Louisiana, Goldsboro, North Carolina and Waukesha, Wisconsin factories with modest CapEx; he expects 2028 financials 'materially better' than the incremental revenue and margin projected in October. Without the former JV's North America exclusivity, GE Vernova booked $800 million of orders into North America from its international transformer factories year to date through 2Q.
quarterly_data.figure: India HVDC project almost $1.5 billion, order in fourth quarter; $800 million of North America orders from international factories year to date

quarterly_data.quarter: GE Vernova Morgan Stanley laguna conference 2026 (09-16-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Wind (CEO Scott Strazik): onshore wind order intake remains soft (tariffs, Section 232 classifications, permitting) and is not expected to change in the third quarter, though second-half orders will be 'materially larger' than first-half; the biggest opportunity is repowering - over 30 gigawatts of GE Vernova's U.S. installed base has repowering potential, with Production Tax Credits expiring at the end of 2030. Wind profitability will be much better in the second half than the first and in 2027 than 2026, helped by closing out existing offshore projects and improving onshore services. Capital allocation: cash of $13 billion at end of Q2; wants more M&A 'almost certainly ... within our core' with technology differentiation, but will be patient.
quarterly_data.figure: over 30 gigawatts of U.S. installed base with repowering potential; cash $13 billion
